extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers (computational algebra / mathematicians using the GAP system)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP operations, attributes, and properties related to collections, lists, enumerators, iterators, and domains; specifies required argument shapes, return behavior, mutability, sortedness, and performance/implementation notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CollectionsFamily / CollectionsFamily(Fam)
rubrics_metrics.description: All collections of elements in the family Fam form the new family CollectionsFamily(Fam).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CollectionsFamily describes relations between an element and collections of elements in the same family; used to create families of collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCollectionFamily
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCollectionFamily(obj) is true if Fam is a family of collections, and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect whether an object is a collections family; ElementsFamily assumes the family was constructed by CollectionsFamily and stores the original elements family.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementsFamily
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementsFamily(Fam) returns the family from which Fam was created by CollectionsFamily; signals an error if Fam is not a collections family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction of a collections family always stores its elements family; example usage shown in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: CategoryCollections
rubrics_metrics.description: CategoryCollections(filter) returns the collections category of filter, a category true for all elements in CollectionsFamily(Fam) if filter is true for all elements of Fam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works only if the collections category is created before the collections family; recommended to construct collections categories immediately after the underlying category.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareCategoryCollections
rubrics_metrics.description: DeclareCategoryCollections(name) calls CategoryCollections on the category bound to global variable name and binds the result to a global variable with a derived name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming conventions for resulting global variable are described (e.g., Something Collection -> Something CollColl).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsListOrCollection
rubrics_metrics.description: IsListOrCollection(obj) is a supercategory of IsList and IsCollection, used to describe arguments for functions defined for both lists and collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for functions like Intersection, Iterator, Random; indicates argument may be a list (possibly with holes) or a collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerator
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerator(listorcoll) returns an immutable list enum. For lists enum contains elements (and holes) in same order; for non-list collections enum contains different elements in an unspecified order (may change between calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: enum[pos] may not be constant-time; size in memory is kept as small as feasible. Default method for lists is Immutable; no default for non-list collections. Use Enumerator when you need an immutable snapshot; examples show non-constant-time and mutability properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnumeratorSorted
rubrics_metrics.description: EnumeratorSorted(listorcoll) returns an immutable list of the different elements in sorted order w.r.t. <. Argument must be a collection or list whose elements lie in the same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length is number of different elements. enum[pos] may not execute in constant time; memory kept small. Use when a sorted immutable enumerator is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnumeratorByFunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: EnumeratorByFunctions(D_or_Fam, record) returns an immutable, dense, duplicate-free list enum whose Length, element access, Position, and IsBound can be implemented by user-provided functions in record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record must provide ElementNumber and NumberElement; if first argument is a family, Length must be provided. Optional components: IsBound[], Membership, AsList, ViewObj, PrintObj. It is not checked that the result is duplicate-free or dense. The record is modified in place; consider setting additional properties (e.g., IsSSortedList) after construction. If you implement a method for Enumerator, also install for EnumeratorSorted.

rubrics_metrics.name: List (for a collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: List(C) for a collection C that is not a list returns a new mutable list new with length equal to number of different elements of C and containing those elements in an unspecified order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: new[pos] executes in constant time and size is proportional to its length. Generic method is ShallowCopy( Enumerator(C) ). Developers can install methods for ListOp to adapt behavior for custom types.

rubrics_metrics.name: SortedList / SortedListBy
rubrics_metrics.description: SortedList(listorcoll[, func]) returns a new mutable dense list with elements in sorted order w.r.t. < or func. SortedListBy(listorcoll, func) orders elements so func(new[i]) <= func(new[i+1]) and computes func(listorcoll[i]) once and stores results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument must be a collection or list whose elements lie in the same family. new[pos] executes in constant time; memory proportional to length. SortedListBy can be more efficient than two-argument Sort because func is computed once per element.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSortedList / Set
rubrics_metrics.description: SSortedList(listorcoll[, fun]) returns a new dense, mutable, duplicate-free list of different elements in strictly sorted order w.r.t. \<. If fun is provided, it is applied to elements and resulting values are used for strict sorting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument must be a collection or list; comparisons must make values comparable via \<. Set is a synonym. new[pos] executes in constant time; memory proportional to length.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsList
rubrics_metrics.description: AsList(listorcoll) returns an immutable list imm: for lists it preserves elements (and holes) in order; for non-list collections it returns different elements in an unspecified order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: imm[pos] executes in constant time; use AsList if mutability is not needed. If many element tests are expected, consider AsSSortedList instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsSortedList
rubrics_metrics.description: AsSortedList(listorcoll) returns a dense, immutable list imm containing elements in sorted order w.r.t. <=. Argument elements must lie in same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only difference to SortedList is immutability. imm[pos] executes in constant time; memory proportional to length.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsSSortedList / AsSet
rubrics_metrics.description: AsSSortedList(listorcoll) (AsSet synonym) returns a dense, immutable, duplicate-free list of different elements in strictly sorted order w.r.t. \<. Argument elements must lie in same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons for sorting can be expensive; use AsList if sortedness is not required. Unlike many other set-returning functions, AsSSortedList must return the proper set (not a domain object).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements(C) does the same as AsSSortedList: returns a strictly sorted list of elements of C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported for backward compatibility. If sortedness is not needed, AsList is recommended; if strictly sorted 'set' is needed prefer AsSet or AsSSortedList.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsEmpty
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEmpty(listorcoll) returns true if the collection or list contains no elements, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple property used to detect empty lists/collections; examples show usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFinite
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFinite(C) returns true if collection C is finite, false otherwise. Default method checks Size(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods for IsFinite may call Size, but Size must not call IsFinite. Default implementation uses Size; implementors should be careful about mutual calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTrivial
rubrics_metrics.description: IsTrivial(C) returns true if collection C consists of exactly one element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used with IsNonTrivial which is defined in terms of IsTrivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNonTrivial
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNonTrivial(C) returns true if collection C is empty or consists of at least two elements (i.e., not exactly one element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined as the negation of IsTrivial in the sense given; examples illustrate behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsWholeFamily
rubrics_metrics.description: IsWholeFamily(C) returns true if collection C contains the whole family of its elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior for Int vs modular rings and free groups; used to detect whether a collection represents its entire underlying family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size
rubrics_metrics.description: Size(listorcoll) returns the size of the list or collection, either an integer or infinity. For lists it is the Length. Default method checks the length of an enumerator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods for IsFinite may call Size, but Size must not call IsFinite. Use Size to get numerical/infinite size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative(C) returns a representative element of collection C; it is free in choosing which element and may return different values across calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative aims for a cheap-to-compute element; unlike Random it does not try to distribute answers. For domains, methods try to fetch from known generator lists but do not compute generators; Representative may error if no generators stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: RepresentativeSmallest
rubrics_metrics.description: RepresentativeSmallest(C) returns the smallest element in collection C w.r.t. ordering \<; defaults to comparing all elements but better methods may be installed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when a canonical smallest representative is required; example demonstrates behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubset
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSubset(C1, C2) returns true if C2 is a subset of C1 (each element of C2 is also an element of C1), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaves as if implemented via IsSubsetSet(AsSSortedList(C1), AsSSortedList(C2)) but may work for infinite collections and usually faster. Either argument may be a proper set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection / Intersection2
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection(C1, C2, ...) returns the set of elements that lie in every argument collection. Intersection(list) accepts a list of collections. Intersection2(C1, C2) is the two-argument operation called by Intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each argument may be a homogeneous list not a proper set (Set applied silently). If result is a list it is new and mutable. Methods for Intersection2 should preserve structure where possible (e.g., intersection of two permutation groups returned as a group). Examples show interactions with infinite domains and when one argument is not a group leading to set return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union / Union2
rubrics_metrics.description: Union(C1, C2, ...) returns the set of elements that lie in any of the argument collections. Union(list) accepts a list of collections. Union2(C1, C2) is the two-argument operation called by Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each argument may be a homogeneous list not a proper set (Set applied silently). Result lists are new and mutable. When computing unions of small integer ranges, tries to return result as a range and avoid expanding input ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference(C1, C2) returns the set difference of C1 and C2: elements in C1 but not in C2. Either argument may be a homogeneous list (Set applied silently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C2 need not be a subset of C1; elements of C2 not in C1 are ignored. Result list is new and mutable if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership (\in)
rubrics_metrics.description: \in(obj, C) returns true if obj lies in collection C, false otherwise. The infix 'obj in C' calls this operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods can be installed; examples show membership tests for integers and group elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random
rubrics_metrics.description: Random(listorcoll) returns a pseudo-random element of a dense, nonempty list or a nonempty collection. Random(from, to) returns a random integer in the inclusive range for arbitrary integers from and to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution depends on argument: dense list => uniform; finite collections usually uniform; infinite collections 'reasonable' distribution per collection-specific rules. Global random generator is used and initialized deterministically at GAP start (so runs are reproducible). For speed-over-quality, use PseudoRandom; see Random methods that take random source as first arg for more control. Behavior undefined for empty or non-dense lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PseudoRandom
rubrics_metrics.description: PseudoRandom(listorcoll) returns a pseudo random element; for lists behaves like Random, but for non-list collections returned elements need not be equally distributed — emphasis on cheap-to-compute elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when speed prioritized over distribution; Representative returns arbitrary (possibly identical) elements, Random aims for reasonable distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomList
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomList([rs, ]list) returns a (pseudo-)random element with equal distribution from a dense list; optional random source rs may be supplied (defaults to GlobalMersenneTwister).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RandomSource for higher-quality or reproducible sources; examples illustrate usage. Intended for dense lists; uses rs when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterator
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterator(listorcoll) returns a mutable iterator iter that loops over elements of the list or collection without repetition. For lists, iterator yields elements (not holes) in the same order; for non-list collections iterator yields elements in unspecified order (may change between calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterators may not store all elements (useful for infinite domains). Iterator returns a fresh mutable iterator each call; operations on iterators: IsDoneIterator, NextIterator, ShallowCopy. Behavior w.r.t. changes to mutable collections is not defined unless documented; for mutable lists see IteratorList notes. Default implementation for non-list collections is IteratorList(Enumerator(C)); better methods should be provided per collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorSorted
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorSorted(listorcoll) returns a mutable iterator that loops over different elements in sorted order. Argument must be a collection or list whose elements lie in the same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic method for collections is IteratorList(EnumeratorSorted(C)). Use when sorted iteration is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: IsIterator(obj) is a category membership test: every iterator lies in category IsIterator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to check whether an object is an iterator.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDoneIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDoneIterator(iter) returns true if all elements have been returned already by NextIterator(iter), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to check loop termination when using NextIterator directly; part of iterator protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: NextIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: NextIterator(iter) returns the next element of the iterator iter if IsDoneIterator(iter) is false; behavior undefined if IsDoneIterator(iter) is true (may error or crash).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NextIterator mutates iterator; use IsDoneIterator to guard calls. Examples show while-loop use. Implementations must update iter's state.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorList
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorList(list) returns a new iterator that iterates over elements of the list (which may have holes) in the same order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list is mutable and changed after IteratorList call, changes to positions not yet reached will affect the iterator. Changes also affect shallow copies of the list; implementors should be aware of mutability semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: TrivialIterator(elm) returns a mutable iterator for the one-element collection [elm].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience iterator for trivial collections (IsTrivial).

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorByFunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorByFunctions(record) returns a mutable iterator iter whose NextIterator, IsDoneIterator, and ShallowCopy are implemented by functions in record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record must contain NextIterator, IsDoneIterator, ShallowCopy, optional ViewObj and PrintObj, and any further data components used by these functions. IteratorByFunctions modifies record in place (no shallow copy) and produced iterators lie in filter IsStandardIterator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational structure of domains (domains and elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains are structured sets with an operational structure: a collection of operations under which the domain is closed; elements may admit more operations than those forming the domain structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domains are useful both to represent structured sets and to specify that computations take place in a certain domain (many functions accept an optional domain argument). The manual points out examples and that elements exist independently of domains; domains are often constructed by domain constructors.
